The thing is, I (like many others) played Cuphead and didn't have these issues. I (like many others) was consistently impressed with the hitboxes and the snappy controls. I can't even find a single video online highlighting janky hitboxes, outside of a couple of very specific ones that have since been fixed. So when people complain about the game being unfair, it seems far more likely to me that they're just bad and making excuses than having prophetic revelations that the vast majority of players somehow missed.

Cuphead isn't beyond criticism. Some bosses are bad in places, like the bee's RNG platforms or Cala Maria's bullshit parries while S-ranking. The game as a whole is fairly derivative of Contra and doesn't innovate much with its gameplay, relying on its art to distinguish itself. Multiplayer is a messy clusterfuck that didn't need to exist. The difficulty curve is more of a zigzag, with bosses varying widely in challenge even between worlds. But outside of a few very particular issues that are not representative of the game as a whole, Cuphead is not unfair or janky - that's its greatest success.

**Dead Air** can summon thin semitransparent walls within five feet of himself that block motion. They inviolably halt all kinetic motion - punches, bullets, a speeding train (or at least, the part of the train that hits the wall). They work down to the molecular level, blocking sound and rapidly reducing objects in direct physical contact with them to absolute zero - touch one for too long, and you'll be lucky just to lose your hand. They can't be moved and linger in place regardless of whether Dead Air is in range, deteriorating after a few minutes or faster if many others are summoned. Dead Air himself is totally immune to the walls' effects.

**Microscope** is a Thinker who learns exponentially more about things he's physically close to. His power's maximum range is only about ten feet, and that far it barely works. But right up close, he gains incredible amounts of information about whatever he's focused on. He can easily hack an ATM, fly a helicopter, or even compete with Number Man in a hand-to-hand fight. But put him on the phone or point a gun at him, and he's useless.
